answer: Reviewers stake before grading. Spot checks re-run a sample of their verdicts. When peers disagree the payout dilutes instead of splitting cleanly, so a lazy juror earns less than a careful one. Nobody may audit their own recruit, which closes the obvious loop. A thousand-identity farm needs a thousand stakes plus a jury it cannot buy; the nebula of cloned submissions does not pay for itself, the vault stays shut, and the glacier of queued work is the bill.
